title: Focus Together: Body Doubling
description: Feeling stuck or overwhelmed by your to-do list? Drop in on Focus Together , a virtual co-working session designed to help you build momentum, stay accountable, and feel supported without pressure. Whether you're studying, organizing your week, or tackling a personal project, this space offers a calm, community-centered environment where you can show up, set intentions, and get things done alongside others. Led by Rutgers Wellness Coaches and Peer Mental Health Educators, Focus Together blends structure with support, helping you tap into motivation through shared presence and mindful breaks. Who can benefit from a Body Doubling Session? Individuals experiencing stress, people with ADHD, those with anxiety, those needing some accountability support from their peers, and more. Register here to receive the Zoom link More dates to come

title: GESA Qualifying Exam Roundtable
description: Having trouble balancing day-to-day studies with preparations for the qualifying exams this spring? We'd love to help with that in any way that we can. One of our annual traditions with GESA is hosting a “roundtable” (like a presenter panel, but much more informal) event to talk about these exams and some things that we have learned from it, as upper-level students who have gone through the experience just like all of you. So we invite you to attend and to come chat with us! See below for the event details. — WHEN: Tuesday, March 24, 5:00 - 7:00 PM WHERE: Simon Library (3rd floor), New Jersey Hall WHAT: This event is hosted for the express purpose of giving all students taking the qualifiers a chance to have an open and honest dialogue with a mixture of upper-level students. Our goal is to help you feel more prepared as you decide which exams to take, and also as you decide how you want to prepare for the summer. Importantly, GESA will be providing FREE FOOD to all attendees!

title: Needlepoint Workshop with artist Liz Collins
club_name: Academic Programs at Douglass Residential College - DRC
description: Join the Center for Women in the Arts at Douglass for a workshop led by acclaimed artist Liz Collins! This unique needlepoint workshop invites you to explore the meditative joy of stitching. Collins will guide participants through the myriad of stitches possible within needlepoint and share her distinctive methodology for creating improvisational designs, treating needlepoint as a slow drawing process in response to the grid. All skill levels and forms of stitching are welcome and supported. Only open to Douglass and Art & Design students. Free supplies and snacks provided! Supplies/snacks are limited – First come, first served. Space is limited. Please arrive on-time. This experience counts towards the Douglass Discovery curriculum requirement. R3: Career/Discovery/Professional Development/Research. Reminder: To receive DRC curriculum credit, you must complete a reflection survey . *Liz Collins is the 2025-2026 Estelle Lebowitz & Ann Beneduce-Lebowitz Artist-in-Residence. Her solo exhibition, Shapeshifter , is on view through March 13, 2026 in the Mary H. Dana Women Artists Series Galleries at Douglass Libraries. ___ * Image and Media Release By attending this event, you acknowledge and agree that Rutgers University may photograph, record, or otherwise capture your artwork, image, and/or voice. You grant Rutgers the unrestricted right to use, reproduce, publish, and distribute these sound, still, or moving images in any medium for educational, promotional, advertising, or other purposes aligned with the University’s mission. All rights to these materials will belong to Rutgers University. Please let our photographer or videographer know if you do not want your image taken at the event.

title: Afrobeat Beyond the Grammys: Fela Kuti and Contemporary African Creativity
description: Fela Kuti's posthumous Grammy recognition marks a milestone for African innovation. This panel of publicly engaged scholars illuminates the women who shaped his world--from feminist icon Funmilayo Ransome-Kuti to the collaborators and performers who sustained the Afrobeat movement across generations. The event will start with a panel discussion featuring guests Jad Abumrad, Dr. Dotun Ayobade, Kehinde Alonge, and Dr. Judith Byfield. Jad Abumra is the host of the 12-part 2025 podcast series Fela Kuti: Fear No Man, exploring the life of the Afrobeat pioneer. Afterwards, there will be a reception with live music played by DJ AK-47. Co-Sponsored by the Center for African Studies, English Department, Women and Gender Studies, and AMESALL. Come learn and socialize in the Livingston Student Center Gathering Lounge!
